messages:
Kenji Nakamura: Dropping latest results dashboard mockups for route-level A/B experiments. Would love eyes esp on confidence indicators + error-rate viz. Figma: https://figma.com/file/RI-AB-Results-Dashboard (page: “Results v3”) and quick export: https://drive.google.com/redwood/ab-testing-dashboard-mockups#slide=7

Kenji Nakamura: Context: this is the main “Experiment results” view in Console. Top: exposures + split, then latency/cost/error tiles, then “Quality (optional)” section if eval suite attached.

Tessa Morgan: Thanks Kenji. Overall layout feels solid.

Tessa Morgan: Biggest question: what are we trying to communicate with the confidence pill? Right now it reads like “High confidence” == safe to ship, which we probably can’t guarantee.

Tessa Morgan: I’d rather phrase it as “Statistical strength” or “Evidence” and make it super clear it’s about uncertainty, not endorsement.

Marissa Cole: +1. We’ve been getting questions from design partners that interpret “confidence” as an SLA / guardrail signal.

Dylan Brooks: Yeah, and SRE is also asking for guardrail regressions to be the thing that triggers rollback, not a stats badge.

Allison Grant: From observability POV, I’m worried the badge is too binary. We should avoid a single green dot because folks will miss the error-rate spike right below.

Allison Grant: Also, error rate tile is currently a small line + delta. Can we make it more obvious when it’s spiking, even if volume is low?

Kenji Nakamura: That’s fair. The current thought was:
- “High” if sample size > X and CI doesn’t overlap 0 for primary metric
- “Medium/Low” otherwise
But I agree the wording is dangerous.

Sana Farid: If we keep anything like that, we need to be precise. “CI doesn’t overlap 0” depends on what metric/diff we’re showing and the test. Also, we’ll have multiple metrics (latency, cost, error, eval score). One badge can’t represent all of that.

Sana Farid: Suggest: show uncertainty on each metric (e.g., CI whiskers on delta) and remove the global “confidence” pill entirely for v1.

Tessa Morgan: +1 removing global pill. If we really need an at-a-glance thing, maybe “Data volume: insufficient / adequate” with an info tooltip.

Marissa Cole: Product-wise we can live without the pill in beta. What we can’t lose is a way to prevent misreads.

Sean Gallagher: +100 on misreads. In incidents we’ve seen teams chase “latency improved” while error rate quietly doubled. If we’re giving a summary at all, it needs to surface regressions loudly.

Sean Gallagher: Also pls consider error type breakdown (429 vs 5xx vs timeouts). When routing shifts capacity, 429 is the one we care about first.

Kenji Nakamura: Re error tile: I was trying to keep the first screen light, but maybe the error tile should be “Error rate + error budget burn” style?

Allison Grant: You don’t need burn for v1, but:
- make error rate a top-row tile alongside latency/cost
- show absolute + delta
- show CI / uncertainty if sample is small
- add a stacked breakdown on hover or in the detail drawer

Nadia Rahman: +1 to absolute + delta. We’ve had folks look only at % delta and miss that baseline was 0.02% -> 0.04% (looks like 2x, but maybe not material) vs 1% -> 2% (material). Both should look different.

Chloe Martin: From implementation side, we can support breakdown by standardized error classes (timeout, rate_limited, upstream_5xx, client_4xx). But please don’t make it arbitrary strings, we’re enforcing tag allowlists.

Tessa Morgan: Visual thought: for error rate, consider a “small multiples” sparkline for A and B rather than a single line. It makes it easier to see volatility + which variant is spiking.

Kenji Nakamura: Like two lines with legend “Control / Variant” ?

Tessa Morgan: Either two lines in same chart (color-coded) or literally two tiny aligned charts. If accessibility is a concern, aligned charts can be easier.

Allison Grant: If same chart, please don’t rely only on red/green. Use patterns or distinct markers. Also error rate often sits near zero; consider y-axis handling. A log scale might confuse people.

Sana Farid: Strong preference: keep linear but show “% of requests” + include a “not enough data” state. If we show confidence/CI, the right thing is a binomial CI (Wilson / Agresti-Coull) per variant, then CI on the diff is trickier.

Sana Farid: At minimum: show counts. “Errors: 3 / 12,340” next to the rate.

Marissa Cole: Counts next to rate would be great. Customers keep asking “how many actual failures is this?”

Dylan Brooks: Agree. Also, can we surface “exposures” vs “requests”? For streaming, we might have multiple events per request and it gets confusing.

Chloe Martin: In the dashboard we should stick to “requests” as the unit for error rate and latency. Exposures are a separate thing (assignment logged per request). We can label top as “Requests assigned” to avoid confusion.

Kenji Nakamura: Got it. I’ll update copy.

Kenji Nakamura: On confidence indicators: sounds like direction is to remove the global badge and instead add per-metric uncertainty / “insufficient data” messaging.

Tessa Morgan: Yep. Also for the delta table, I’d like a clearer visual hierarchy:
- Show absolute values for Control and Variant
- Show delta as secondary (and only color delta)
- Add tooltips: what’s being compared, time window, filters applied.

Allison Grant: And please add an obvious filter chip row (region, route, model version, time window). People will screenshot without realizing they’re filtered.

Kenji Nakamura: It’s in the mockup as a dropdown top right; I can move it into chips.

Sean Gallagher: Another SRE request: error-rate visualization should make it super clear if the experiment is violating guardrails. Even if the results page is “analysis”, operators will look here during incidents.

Sean Gallagher: Could we add a “Guardrail status” banner when thresholds exceeded (latency p95 regression > X%, error rate > Y%) with link to rollback action?

Marissa Cole: We have that in the runbook flow, but not on results. Might be good to show read-only status at least. (Actions are permissioned.)

Dylan Brooks: We can do a banner that reads from the guardrail evaluator state. Probably Beta+1, but we can stub copy now.

Kenji Nakamura: Cool. I’ll add a banner placeholder to the layout.

Nadia Rahman: One more: cost tile. It shows “$/1k requests” in the mockup; would be better as “$/1M tokens” or “$/request” depending on route. Otherwise it’ll vary wildly with prompt length.

Marissa Cole: For beta we promised token-level cost. Let’s show: “Cost per 1k output tokens” and “Cost per request” as toggle?

Sana Farid: Careful with too many toggles. But yes, cost per token is more comparable across variants.

Kenji Nakamura: Makes sense. I’ll adjust.

Tessa Morgan: Summary of feedback I’m hearing:
1) Remove/rename global confidence badge (avoid implying “safe”) 
2) Add per-metric uncertainty + “insufficient data” states
3) Error rate: make top-level, show absolute+delta+counts, consider variant breakdown
4) Improve filters visibility + screenshot safety
5) Consider guardrail status banner (read-only at least)

Kenji Nakamura: Confirmed. I’ll push a v4 later today and tag folks here.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: When you update, can you also add an example of a low-volume experiment state? That’s where uncertainty + error counts matter most.

Kenji Nakamura: Yep, will add a “low traffic” mock state (e.g., 1.2k req total) and show the “insufficient data” message.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks. And pls keep the “error type breakdown” in the detail drawer even if not on the main tile.

Chloe Martin: +1, detail drawer works. We can query breakdown by standardized classes without blowing up cardinality.

Marissa Cole: Appreciate all. Kenji, once updated can we link in DES-143? I want to close the loop there.

Kenji Nakamura: Will do. Posting v4 in DES-143 + here once it’s ready.
